newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK silver coin sells for more than $100,000.
newsitem.headline: HK silver coin sells for more than $100,000.

text.p: An undated silver Hong Kong dollar coin bearing the bust of British Queen Victoria was sold for HK$828,000 (US$108,000) at an auction here, London-based auctioneer Spink & Sons Ltd said on Monday.
The auctioned price was well above the expected HK$600,000 to HK$750,000, it said in a statement.
The second highest price of the auction went for a 1929 silver dollar coin showing the bust of Sun Yet Sen, founder of modern China, at HK$483,000, it said.
Total sales during the day amounted to HK$11.7 million compared to last year's auction of HK$9.24 million, it said.
The top-selling banknote was a Hongkong and Shanghai Bank $5 note, dated May 1, 1884, which sold for HK$356,500, the auctioneer said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule in 1997.
